holidays.name: World UFO Day
holidays.description: Skywatchers around the globe spend the evening scanning the heavens for flying saucers, mysterious lights, and anything that might be waving back. It's a night for blankets, binoculars, and big cosmic questions.
holidays.origin: The date is commonly tied to the anniversary of the alleged 1947 Roswell incident in New Mexico. Some UFO enthusiasts instead celebrate on June 24, but July 2 is the date most widely observed.
holidays.funFact: The Roswell incident that inspired the day began with ranch debris in 1947. The military first described it as a crashed 'flying disc' and then quickly switched to calling it a weather balloon.

holidays.name: National Disco Day
holidays.description: Break out the sequins, platform shoes, and mirror ball. This day is a reason to hit the dance floor and play your favorite groovy hits from the 1970s.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the music and dance culture that took over clubs and radio in the 1970s.
holidays.funFact: Disco's heyday gave us the 12-inch single, which was designed so DJs could keep dancers moving with longer, louder mixes.

holidays.name: I Forgot Day
holidays.description: This is a day to admit that you've forgotten something, whether it's a name, an errand, or why you walked into the room. It's a gentle reminder that nobody remembers everything.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, and it's now listed on many July calendars.
holidays.funFact: The 'doorway effect' is a well-known memory quirk. Walking through a doorway can make your brain file away what you were thinking about, which is why you forget why you entered a room.
